scope: State serialization/projection and feature ownership-index audit; not a whole-release freeze or external Jev verdict

targetedTests.command: npm test -- tests/unit/state-store.test.ts tests/unit/feature-state-validation.test.ts tests/unit/agent-binding.test.ts tests/unit/message-bus.test.ts tests/unit/task-runtime.test.ts

invariants: Commit mutex and full canonical/schema validation retained before publication.
A successful durable commit is published only after journal write and fsync; failure blocks subsequent commits.
Compaction failure after journal durability retains the committed transaction, marks recovery required, and does not claim rollback.
Projected reads and returned commit states are detached copies; escaping mutation drafts cannot change private state.
Initial journal directory entry is fsynced through atomicStateFile before the first append.
Initialization and recovery-transform failures clean up this process-owned inode; replacement owner files are preserved.
Version-1 canonical snapshot/journal format and state/entry checksums remain compatible.
Feature task/delegation associations remain complete, unique, and same-task after replacing nested scans with Set lookups.
limitations: Synthetic memory-only store timings exclude the business schema validator; feature-state validation is measured separately.
No claims about durable NAS fsync latency, end-to-end agent/model latency, token savings, or OS adversarial filesystem isolation.
Caching canonical JSON adds O(B) retained memory for validated state size B; no peak-memory reduction was measured.
Projection reduces copied data but message pull still scans/sorts indexed messages and retains an overall state size cap.
